newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy could up global ENI offer later today.
newsitem.headline: Italy could up global ENI offer later today.

text.p: Italy's Treasury could announce a decision to increase the overall scale of its offering of shares in state energy corporation ENI later today or on Friday, a Treasury source said.
The Treasury said on Wednesday that it would substantially increase the amount of ENI shares being offered to the Italian public in response to strong demand but did not say by how much.
It also said it was considering an increase in the overall number of shares it would offer to all investors.
Of the total 700 million shares currently on offer, some 300 million are being offered to Italian retail investors, 235 to institutional investors and 165 million to investors in the United States.
The Treasury said on Wednesday demand was double the amount on offer to the public after only three days.

Global coordinators for the sale, Italian investment bank IMI and CS First Boston, have been granted an over-allotment or "green-shoe" option of a further 105 million shares which will be offered to institutional investors in the case of heavy demand.
The Treasury has said previously that the offer, which accounts for 8.75 percent of ENI's share capital, or 10 percent if the green shoe is included, could be increased if demand was strong enough.
The Treasury sold the first 15 percent tranche of ENI shares in November 1995 at 5,250 lire a share to trade in Milan, London and New York. The issue raised 6.3 trillion lire.
Public subscription to the offer in Italy runs from October 21 to October 25 and the final share price will be fixed on October 26 with trading expected to start on October 28.
The Treasury has said the public offer will be priced at either 7,425 lire or at Friday's closing price minus a 3.5 percent discount, whichever is lower.
ENI shares were quoted at 7,385 lire on the Milan bourse at mid-session on Thursday.
